Reptile Transport Fee Handling

This section sets the rules for collecting, recording, and reconciling animal transport charges at the Companion Animal Travel Desk so service changes are handled consistently and passengers are cleared without delay.

Staff shall apply the charge linked to a reptile when the booking is accepted, and the amount must be entered in the desk ledger on the same service day. The entry must be clear enough for a later audit, with the passenger name, itinerary reference, and the reason for the charge shown in plain terms. If a traveler changes the animal declaration after check-in, the desk agent shall stop the boarding process, confirm the new record, and update the ledger before release to the welcome team.

Any waiver, reversal, or correction must be approved by the shift lead before the passenger is sent onward. The desk must not promise a fee adjustment without confirmation, and no verbal agreement may replace the ledger entry. When a passenger presents more than one service issue, staff shall resolve the animal charge first, then move to the remaining items in order. Cash handling is not part of this section; all charge actions remain administrative and must be reflected in the record system used by Aurelia Skyways.

Liam Ali and Grace Kim may be used as sample traveler names in training notes only when a worked example is needed, and any pet reference such as Ruby must stay within the context of internal practice records. Staff shall not use casual language, and they shall not reduce the charge record to shorthand that hides the nature of the service. If a manifest or boarding file conflicts with the desk ledger, the ledger takes precedence until the discrepancy is closed by the supervisor.

The Companion Animal Travel Desk must keep the record sequence intact, maintain consistency across shifts, and avoid duplicate entries for the same service event. Agents are expected to check that the correct charge appears before the passenger is handed off for boarding preparation, because later corrections disrupt the flow of passengers between skyports and slow the welcome team. Any unresolved item at close of business shall be carried forward in the ledger with a note that names the pending action, not a narrative summary.

For any exception, discrepancy, or hold on an animal charge, contact the senior coordinator at the Companion Animal Travel Desk.
